questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Career opportunities

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: I would like to explore the opportinuty to work in China after my education.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: I would say the THU is a great place to be, IF you are extremely open minded and proactive. Some clubs such as the marching band, piano clubs etc are not open to exchange students. Some sports teams are also closed off. I have had the honor to join the schools skiing team as one of the only exchange students, but that was the exception, not the rule. In general, talking to people, even on the streets, is extremely rewarding and is recommended from my part to get to know people.

questions.question: How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: Not that easy. The essential information given was quite alright, although the ones you need for a fulfilling exchange is something you need to figure out yourself.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: Orientation and arrival assitance mostly, where they will tell you about you dorm, the rules, the cantines etc.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
questions.answer: Most of the useful information is given verbally through students, that is why getting to know people, especially the locals asap is very important. I would perhaps even say skipping the orientation for some club activities is preferable.

questions.question: How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing through my host institution

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: On campus

questions.question: What options were available for on campus housing? *
questions.answer: single dorm, 2 man dorm and 3 man dorm.

questions.question: What options were available for meal plans or cooking facilities? *
questions.answer: Common kitchen.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about on campus housing? *
questions.answer: Nothing particular.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: It is kinda the same as in UCPH, where you register courses online through a portal. There are multiple periods of registration, and you can also drop courses after they have begun.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: Teachers are extremely helpful to exchange students, get in contact with the teach asap.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: This is where the problem comes in. Most of the courses provided on the excel sheet you receive prior to the stay is NOT available to exchange students.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: 1. Ask for the final list of courses available for exchange students. 2. Ask the course professor if he/she could add you in as an extra if you did not get your relevant course.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA courses at your host university? *
questions.answer: Both

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: Due to the fact that most "good" courses are not available to exchange students, the level of the courses is debatable. The teaching method is vastly different, as you are required to meetup. It is hard to explain, but expect a lot more "discussion" type courses then pure math, which is what I am enrolled into.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: Different. UCPH math courses are very much theoretical with hardcore calculations. While in THU it is more discussion and understanding based.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer: Coporate Finance, Econometrics, PE and VC, Public Leader Dialogue, Life Insurance, International Economics.

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: To be fair, none in particular, unless it is something your are interested in and have not had something similar before.

questions.answer: Medical costs, as they are not covered by your insurance.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: Hobby activities such as skiing, rowing etc.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: This was the best part, you would not want to go back to UCPH after a semester here, since the campus life is so good.

questions.question: What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: I am mostly into sports, and there are so many of them. It depends on your interest mostly, as you can definitely find something related to it. Some clubs, as said before, are a bit more closed off, and you would either need to be extremely good or extremely lucky in order to get in.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Be active in the clubs, they are the most rewarding thing on you exchange stay.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Join the club excursions, that is where you will get to know people.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: I have a chinese background, so very easy. However, for non chinese, I would assume a bit harder, as most stuff in written in chinese, with english translations in between.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Just talk to them, they are very friendly in general. Some of my best friends obtained here was through talking to them on the streets or on the soccer field, while playing sports.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: None in particular.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: The helpfulness and "team" sense.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer: Be proactive x3. This is the single most important thing. As in China, nothing will come to you if you are not proactive.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: Come a bit earlier, so that you can get you bank, phone etc in order.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: The clubs hands down. You get a sense of belonging there. The friends I made are the most rewarding part of the exchange.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: Nothing in particular.

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
